questions.explanation: B is correct. OSTENTATIOUS = making an exaggerated display of wealth or knowledge to impress others. Antonym = UNPRETENTIOUS = modest, not trying to impress. Trap: Flamboyant, Pompous, Extravagant are all synonyms (showy/elaborate) — the distractor cluster is the synonym group.

B is correct. VINDICTIVE = having or showing a strong or unreasonable desire for revenge. Antonym = MERCIFUL = showing compassion/forgiveness, especially to an offender. Trap: Spiteful, Resentful, Vengeful are all synonyms of vindictive — each indicates desire to cause harm or seek revenge.

C is correct. PERFIDIOUS = guilty of betrayal or treachery. Antonym = FAITHFUL = remaining loyal and true. Trap: Treacherous, Deceitful, Duplicitous are synonyms (all mean deceptive or disloyal). Root trick: 'perfid-' comes from Latin 'perfidia' = bad faith; its antonym must denote good faith = faithful.

C is correct. EPHEMERAL = lasting for a very short time. Antonym = ENDURING = lasting over a long period; permanent. Trap: Fleeting, Transitory, Momentary are all synonyms (all mean short-lived). The '-epi-' (on) + '-hemera-' (day) Greek roots help: ephemeral = lasts only one day. Opposite = lasts much longer = enduring/perpetual.

D is correct. IGNOBLE = not honourable in character or purpose; base or vile. Antonym = HONOURABLE = bringing or worthy of honour and respect. Trap: Dishonourable and Contemptible are synonyms; Magnanimous (generous in forgiving) is not the direct antonym of ignoble, though it is a positive trait.

C is correct. VERBOSE = using or expressed in more words than are needed; long-winded. Antonym = TERSE = sparing in the use of words; brief and concise. Trap: Wordy, Garrulous, Loquacious are all synonyms of verbose (all mean talking too much). SSC frequently tests the synonyms and antonyms of VERBOSE — also know: laconic, pithy, succinct as antonyms.

C is correct. IMPERIOUS = assuming power or authority without justification; arrogant and domineering. Antonym = HUMBLE = having or showing a modest opinion of one's own importance. Trap: Commanding, Overbearing, Domineering are all synonyms (varying degrees of imperious behaviour). Root trick: 'imperium' = power/command; anti-meaning = not commanding = humble.

C is correct. SYCOPHANTIC = behaving or acting in an obsequious way in order to gain advantage; excessively flattering. Antonym = FORTHRIGHT = direct and outspoken; frank (the opposite of using flattery to please). Trap: Obsequious, Fawning, Servile are all synonyms — they all describe excessive deference or flattery. Note: do not confuse 'forthright' with 'forceful' — both start with 'f' but mean different things.

B is correct. MENDACIOUS = not telling the truth; lying. Antonym = VERACIOUS = speaking or representing the truth; truthful. Root trick: 'mendaci-' = lie (Latin), 'verac-' = truth (Latin, also root of 'verify'). Trap: Deceptive, Fraudulent, Duplicitous are synonyms of mendacious (all involve dishonesty). SSC tests mendacious/veracious pair regularly in Tier 2.

C is correct. ACRIMONIOUS = angry and bitter (especially of a speech, argument, or manner). Antonym = CORDIAL = warm and friendly. Trap: Bitter, Rancorous, Caustic are synonyms (acrimonious = bitter; rancorous = resentful; caustic = sharp/biting). Context clue: acrimonious disputes vs. cordial relations — a classic SSC contrast pair.
